name: Area-generic outlet-headroom / drainage-coping indicator over a declared horizon, with refusal

statement.latest: \text{For a declared drainage unit } U \text{ (village, district, province, or sub-basin) with tuple } \langle A_U, O_U, P_U, c_U\rangle \text{ and horizon } H \text{ hours, all quantities on } \mathbb{Q}:\quad R_H(U) := \sum_{o \in O_U} \max(0,\, Q_{cap,o} - Q_{o,now})\cdot H\cdot 3600 \quad D_H(U) := \sum_{t=1}^{H} \Big(\sum_{p \in P_U^{run}} P_{run,p}\Big)\cdot 3600\cdot g_U(t) \quad F_H(U) := c_U\cdot A_U \cdot \sum_{t=1}^{H} rain_t + \sum_{t=1}^{H} Q_{in,up}(t)\cdot 3600 \quad \boxed{S_H(U) := \dfrac{F_H(U)}{\min(D_H(U), R_H(U))}} \text{ with declared tiers OK} (<0.5), \text{TIGHT} (0.5\text{-}1), \text{CRITICAL} (>1); \quad \text{binding}(U) := \arg\min(R_H(U), D_H(U)) \in \{\text{OUTLET}, \text{PUMP}\}, \text{ and per outlet } o: \text{binding}(o) := [R_o = \min_{o'\in O_U} R_{o'}]; \quad \boxed{\text{REFUSED (reason} \in \{\text{UNIT\_NOT\_DECLARED, MISSING\_INPUT, STALE\_INPUT, UNDECLARED\_AREA, UNDECLARED\_EDGE, DERATING\_UNDECLARED}\}\text{)}} \text{ when the tuple is incomplete, any required input is missing/stale/undeclared, or a unit has not declared its derating factor } g_U(t) \text{; } \min(D_H,R_H)=0 \text{ while } F_H>0 \text{ is L5 (system already exceeded), not REFUSED (v2). \quad \text{Urgency: } T_{act}(U):=\min\{t\in\{1,\dots,H\}: F_t(U)\ge\min(D_t(U),R_t(U))\} \text{ (}">H"\text{ if none, reusing PROP-FLOOD-02); combined tier ladder } L_0..L_5,L_R \text{ over } (S_H,T_{act}) \text{, OPEN-for-founder-tuning thresholds, LR (REFUSED) always dominant. Unit } U \text{ MAY be resolved from any } (\text{lat},\text{lon})\in\text{Thailand} \text{ via the graph (basin polygon / nearest reach / pump assets / gauges), each resolved input tagged VERIFIED/RELAYED/INSTINCT, REFUSED (UNIT\_POLYGON\_MISSING, OUTLET\_CAPACITY\_UNKNOWN, NO\_GAUGE\_IN\_UNIT) rather than degraded when unresolved; NO\_PUMPS\_IN\_UNIT is not an error.
statement.note_ascii: For a declared drainage unit U (village, district, province, or sub-basin) with tuple <A_U, O_U, P_U, c_U> and horizon H hours, all on Q: R_H(U) := sum over outlets o in O_U of max(0, Q_cap,o - Q_o,now) * H*3600 (m^3), the total river/outlet headroom over the horizon, summed across every declared downstream receiving reach/sea/reservoir for U (Bangkok has one outlet, Chao Phraya via pumps+Gulf; a village may have one canal/basin outlet; Ayutthaya has one river outlet with no pumps). D_H(U) := sum over hours t=1..H of (sum of running-pump capacities P_run,p for p in P_U) * 3600 * g_U(t) (m^3), the drainage volume clearable by pumps actually running, where g_U(t) in (0,1] is a gravity/pump derating factor: g_U(t)=1 when the outlet's river/tide level is below a declared gravity-threshold, else a declared derating factor (OPEN default=1 with a flag); for a non-tidal outlet g_U(t)=1 by declaration unless the unit separately declares a derating condition. When P_U is empty (no pumps declared for U, e.g. a river-only mainstem town), D_H(U) := 0 by definition, not REFUSED. F_H(U) := c_U * A_U * sum_t rain_forecast(t) (m^3, mm converted to m) + sum_t Q_in,up(t)*3600 (m^3), forecast inflow: the rainfall-runoff term (c_U runoff coefficient DECLARED or, if undeclared, reported as a bound pair [c=0.5, c=1], never a single silent point; A_U catchment area DECLARED with a tag; rain from the nearest official gauges + multi-model ensemble, reported as two readouts, median and max) PLUS an upstream-inflow term Q_in,up(t), the declared flow arriving from upstream graph edges into U (zero when U declares no upstream edge, e.g. Bangkok/Sammakorn; the binding term for a mainstem town like Ayutthaya, which has no rainfall-runoff catchment of consequence relative to river inflow). The indicator S_H(U) := F_H(U) / min(D_H(U), R_H(U)), a finite Q-valued ratio, reported with a declared tier convention (a convention, not a derived boundary): OK if S_H<0.5, TIGHT if 0.5<=S_H<=1, CRITICAL if S_H>1. A separate boolean readout reports which term is binding at unit level, binding(U) in {OUTLET, PUMP} := whichever of R_H(U), D_H(U) is the smaller (the argmin), and per outlet o a second boolean binding(o) := true iff R_o (that outlet's own headroom alone) equals the minimum R_o' across all of U's outlets (identifies which specific outlet is the unit's constraint when U has more than one). REFUSED (reason in {UNIT_NOT_DECLARED, MISSING_INPUT, STALE_INPUT, UNDECLARED_AREA, UNDECLARED_EDGE, DERATING_UNDECLARED}) whenever the declared tuple <A_U, O_U, P_U, c_U> is incomplete (UNIT_NOT_DECLARED), any required reading/declaration is absent (MISSING_INPUT) or a time-varying one is stale (STALE_INPUT), the catchment area is undeclared (UNDECLARED_AREA), an inflow arrives over an undeclared upstream edge (UNDECLARED_EDGE), or a unit has not declared its gravity/tide derating factor g_U(t) (DERATING_UNDECLARED, v2 -- see definitions.g_U(t) and honest_caveats; this replaces the v1 silent default of 1). v2 AMENDMENT: min(D_H,R_H)=0 while F_H>0 is NO LONGER a refusal code (ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW is removed); it is now the L5 tier ("the system is already exceeded", checked after LR but before the ordinary S_H/T_act bands -- see readout_classes.tier_ladder), since it is a genuinely non-evaluable ratio but a valid and important readout for residents, not an input-availability problem. When min(D_H,R_H)=0 and F_H=0 as well, S_H(U):=0 (falls in band L0) is a valid, non-refused readout via the ordinary band rule: no capacity is declared and none is needed. Urgency companion T_act(U) := the smallest hour t<=H at which cumulative F_t(U) reaches min(D_t,R_t) (partial sums through t), directly reusing PROP-FLOOD-02's time-to-threshold construction with a time-varying threshold; reported as the string ">H" when no crossing occurs within the horizon (a determinate, non-refused outcome). The severity band on S_H(U) and the urgency band on T_act(U) are combined into a single declared >=5-level tier ladder L0 (normal) .. L4 (act now) plus L5 (system already exhausted/overtopped, checked before the ratio) and LR (REFUSED, dominant over every numeric band) -- thresholds 0.3/0.6/0.9/1.2 on S_H and 6h/24h/48h on T_act are proposed here and explicitly marked OPEN-for-founder-tuning, not derived. U itself may be RESOLVED from any (lat,lon) in Thailand by walking the water/basin/pump/gauge graph rather than hand-declared: A_U from a basin polygon (VERIFIED) or, absent one, a declared radius-r circle (INSTINCT, r stated) -- else REFUSED UNIT_POLYGON_MISSING; O_U from the nearest reach via HydroRIVERS edges (RELAYED), Q_cap,o from the capacity ledger or else REFUSED OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN for that outlet; P_U from pump_station assets inside A_U, empty being the valid NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT case (D_H:=0, not an error); rain from gauges inside A_U or nearest-k, else REFUSED NO_GAUGE_IN_UNIT; every resolved input carries its VERIFIED/RELAYED/INSTINCT tag, and the whole tier readout is REFUSED, never silently degraded, when a required resolved input has none of these tags.

unit_resolution.input: any (lat, lon) in Thailand -- the drainage unit U is RESOLVED from the graph, never hand-declared, per founder instruction 2026-09-27 ("ทำให้ใช้ได้ทุกละติจูด ลองจิจูดในไทย"); this is the resolver PROP-FLOOD-06 requires before any of R_H/D_H/F_H can be evaluated, and it is itself a total function with its own refusal codes, checked before the ledger arithmetic above
unit_resolution.A_U_resolution: A_U := the sub-basin/basin polygon containing (lat,lon), VERIFIED against a declared basin-polygon layer if one exists in the graph; if only the 22 basin nodes exist WITHOUT polygons, REFUSED (UNIT_POLYGON_MISSING) unless a declared fallback radius-r circle around the point is explicitly opted into, tagged INSTINCT with r stated in the report -- the fallback is never silently substituted
unit_resolution.O_U_resolution: O_U := the downstream reach/canal node(s) reached by walking declared WATER edges from the nearest reach/canal node to (lat,lon) (edges sourced from HydroRIVERS, tagged RELAYED); for each resolved outlet o, Q_cap,o is read from the capacity ledger (e.g. C.29/C.13-adjacent constants) if present, else the outlet is retained in O_U but its headroom term is REFUSED (OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN) rather than silently defaulted
unit_resolution.P_U_resolution: P_U := every pump_station asset whose declared location falls within the resolved A_U, with running/not-running state from the latest available readout; P_U resolving to empty is NOT an error -- it is the declared NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT case and D_H(U):=0 by definition, identical to the Ayutthaya instantiation
unit_resolution.rain_resolution: rain_t at the point is read from official gauges within the resolved A_U (or, if none fall inside A_U, the nearest k gauges outside it, tagged with that fallback) plus the ensemble ensemble forecast evaluated at (lat,lon); no gauge within A_U and no declared nearest-k fallback is REFUSED (NO_GAUGE_IN_UNIT)
unit_resolution.upstream_inflow_resolution: Q_in,up(t) := the reading at the graph edge/gauge entering the resolved A_U from upstream, if the graph declares one; absent declaration, the term is 0 by the same UNDECLARED_EDGE discipline already stated above (never silently non-zero, never silently REFUSED-for-the-whole-unit on this term alone unless the unit's own tuple requires it)
unit_resolution.evidence_tagging: every resolved input is reported with its evidence tag (VERIFIED for a directly gauged/declared reading, RELAYED for a graph-sourced constant such as HydroRIVERS edges or a relayed capacity figure, INSTINCT for a fallback such as the radius-r circle or an untagged derating factor) alongside the numeric value -- the tier readout (see readout_classes.tier_ladder) is REFUSED, never silently degraded to a lower-confidence numeric answer, whenever a required resolved input carries none of these three tags (i.e. is simply missing).
unit_resolution.crs_and_tie_break_defaults: v2 addition (per independent review SHOULD-FIX #9, declared defaults so an implementer never invents these): CRS/projection for interpreting (lat,lon) against the basin-polygon/HydroRIVERS graph is EPSG:4326 (WGS84 geographic) by declared default; a unit MAY declare a different CRS explicitly, tagged accordingly. Tie-break for 'nearest reach' / 'nearest gauge' when a point is equidistant or on a boundary: nearest-k gauges use k=3 within a 10 km radius by declared default, else REFUSED (NO_GAUGE_IN_UNIT); metric is geodesic (great-circle) distance on the declared CRS, not network distance along the water graph (network distance is a stronger, not-yet-declared future refinement, OPEN). When two or more candidates remain exactly tied after distance, the tie-break is the smallest declared asset_id (deterministic, never by name or insertion order).
unit_resolution.staleness_and_ensemble_defaults: v2 addition (per independent review SHOULD-FIX #9): STALE_INPUT windows are declared by default as 3 hours for live/gauged inputs (Q_o,now, pump running-state, gauge levels) and 24 hours for forecast inputs (rain_t, Q_in,up(t) forecasts) -- a reading older than its window is REFUSED (STALE_INPUT), never used past-window. 'The ensemble' in rain_resolution is declared as whichever rainfall-forecast models are actually present in the multimodel forecast files available to the evaluator at run time -- there is no fixed, hand-picked model list; the specific models actually used for a given evaluation MUST be logged in that evaluation's own readout (not silently omitted), so the ensemble composition is always inspectable after the fact even though it is not fixed in this proposal's declaration.

definitions.U: a declared drainage unit: a village, district, province, or sub-basin -- the object is area-generic, not Bangkok-specific; U is defined by its own declared tuple, never inferred from geography
definitions.tuple<A_U,O_U,P_U,c_U>: the required declaration for U: A_U (catchment area, m^2), O_U (outlet set, non-empty for a REFUSED-free evaluation of R_H), P_U (pump set, may be declared empty), c_U (runoff coefficient or bound pair) -- an incomplete tuple is REFUSED UNIT_NOT_DECLARED before any other input is even checked
definitions.O_U: the outlet set for U: one or more downstream receiving reaches/sea/reservoirs, each a declared outlet o with its own Q_cap,o and Q_o,now -- e.g. Bangkok east zone's outlet is Chao Phraya via pumps + the Gulf; Sammakorn village's outlet is Khlong Ban Ma / the retention basin; Ayutthaya's outlet is the Chao Phraya mainstem itself, no pumps
definitions.Q_cap,o: declared conveyance/discharge capacity of outlet o (m^3/s) -- a static declaration with a tag (e.g. 3,000-3,100 m^3/s RELAYED for the Chao Phraya reach at Bangkok, cited from C.29/C.13-adjacent capacity notes); subject only to MISSING_INPUT, never STALE_INPUT
definitions.Q_o,now: the latest gauged flow/level reading at outlet o (m^3/s), e.g. the C.29/C.13 station reading -- time-varying, subject to STALE_INPUT/MISSING_INPUT
definitions.R_H(U): outlet headroom over horizon H: summed across every declared outlet in O_U, max(0, Q_cap,o - Q_o,now)*H*3600 (m^3) -- the volume the river/outlet system could still convey over H hours at its current declared capacity margin, before any pump or rainfall term
definitions.P_U: the pump set for U, each p with a running capacity P_run,p (m^3/s) -- e.g. Sammakorn's ST./SPS pumps; declared empty for a unit with no pumping infrastructure (Ayutthaya mainstem town), in which case D_H(U):=0 by definition, not refused
definitions.g_U(t): gravity/pump derating factor in (0,1] at hour t: 1 when the outlet's river/tide level is below a declared gravity-threshold (drainage runs freely or pumps are unconstrained), else a declared derating factor. v2 AMENDMENT (per independent review SHOULD-FIX): an undeclared g_U(t) is REFUSED (DERATING_UNDECLARED), never silently defaulted to 1 -- this replaces v1's silent OPEN default=1, which was an exception to this proposal's own 'never silently degrade' discipline. A unit MAY explicitly declare g_U(t)=1 (a genuine declaration, not a default): Bangkok's tidal outlet declares g_U(t)=1 for all t with an explicit OPEN tag (no measured tide-interaction curve backs the 1, but it is a stated declaration, not a fallback); a non-tidal outlet (Sammakorn's canal, Ayutthaya's river) likewise declares g_U(t)=1 for all t as its own explicit declaration unless it separately declares a different condition. Any unit that has declared neither a curve nor an explicit g_U(t)=1 is REFUSED (DERATING_UNDECLARED) rather than silently assumed
definitions.D_H(U): drainage volume clearable over H hours: sum over hours of (sum of running pump capacities in P_U) * 3600 * g_U(t) -- zero when P_U is empty
definitions.c_U: runoff coefficient for U, in Q intersect [0,1] -- DECLARED with a source, or, if undeclared, reported as the bound pair [0.5, 1], never a single silent point value (OPEN/INSTINCT until measured for the specific catchment)
definitions.rain_t: forecast rainfall at hour t (mm, converted to m) for U's declared bounding box, from the nearest official gauges plus a multi-model ensemble -- reported as two parallel readouts, the ensemble median and the ensemble max, never collapsed to one number
definitions.Q_in,up(t): declared upstream inflow arriving into U over a declared upstream graph edge (m^3/s) at hour t -- zero when U declares no upstream edge (Bangkok, Sammakorn); the dominant/only inflow term for a mainstem town like Ayutthaya, where the rainfall-runoff term is comparatively negligible; an inflow arriving over an UNdeclared edge is REFUSED UNDECLARED_EDGE, never folded in as zero
definitions.F_H(U): forecast inflow volume over H hours: c_U*A_U*sum(rain_t) + sum(Q_in,up(t)*3600) -- the rainfall-runoff term and the upstream-mainstem term are both present in the general form; either collapses to 0 when U declares no catchment (A_U=0, not applicable) or no upstream edge respectively
definitions.S_H(U): the coping indicator, F_H(U) / min(D_H(U), R_H(U)) -- a finite Q-valued ratio; undefined only in the degenerate case min(D_H,R_H)=0 and F_H>0, which is REFUSED rather than reported as an unbounded number
definitions.OK/TIGHT/CRITICAL: a declared tier convention over S_H(U): OK for S_H<0.5, TIGHT for 0.5<=S_H<=1, CRITICAL for S_H>1 -- these boundaries are a convention this proposal declares, not a derived physical threshold; falsifiable per-unit by observed outcomes (see honest_caveats)
definitions.binding(U): boolean/enum readout, OUTLET if R_H(U) <= D_H(U) else PUMP -- reports which term is the unit-level constraint on min(D_H,R_H); when P_U is empty, binding(U):=OUTLET always (D_H=0 can only bind or tie)
definitions.binding(o): per-outlet boolean readout for each o in O_U: true iff R_o = max(0,Q_cap,o-Q_o,now)*H*3600 is the minimum among all outlets' own headroom terms -- identifies which specific outlet is the constraining one when |O_U|>1; vacuously true for the single outlet when |O_U|=1
definitions.T_act(U): time-to-exhaustion readout, ticks/hours: T_act := min{ t in {1,...,H} : F_t(U) >= min(D_t(U), R_t(U)) } where F_t, D_t, R_t are the same three quantities accumulated only through hour t (partial sums, not the full-H totals) -- the smallest horizon at which cumulative forecast inflow would consume the unit's clearable volume. Directly reuses PROP-FLOOD-02's time-to-threshold construction (T_k := (theta-h(t))*k/Delta_k(t), REFUSED-as-non-value discipline) with theta:=min(D_t,R_t) as a time-varying threshold and h(t):=F_t(U) as the rising series; if the crossing does not occur within the declared horizon H, T_act is reported as the declared string ">H" (a determinate 'not within this horizon', not a numeric extrapolation past H and not REFUSED, since 'not yet reached by hour H' is itself a valid, licensed outcome of the search over t in {1,...,H}).
definitions.C_H(U): v3 NEW: the clearable-volume term actually used in S_H(U) := F_H(U)/C_H(U), replacing the v1/v2 literal min(D_H(U),R_H(U)) wherever that literal expression produced the backtest-found no-pump contradiction (thailand_flood_kg BACKTEST_PROP_FLOOD_06_v0.md sec.2.1, RELAYED: AYUTTHAYA_BANGBAN REFUSED 320/320 rows via the former ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW/L5 branch even though R_H, F_H all resolved, solely because NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT forces D_H:=0, and min(0,R_H)=0 always -- contradicting this proposal's own worked-instantiation table, which stated Ayutthaya reduces to S_H=F_H/R_H). C_H(U) is defined as a total case split on which terms are actually declared for U: (a) NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT (P_U empty) => C_H(U):=R_H(U), terms_present:={R} -- pump term is structurally absent, not zero-and-binding; (b) pumps declared (P_U non-empty) but every outlet in O_U is OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN => C_H(U):=D_H(U), terms_present:={D} -- the outlet term is retained as a PARTIAL flag on the readout (unresolved_terms:={R}), not a whole-unit REFUSED, since D_H alone is still a real, usable clearable-volume readout; (c) both R_H(U) and D_H(U) resolve to real values (pumps declared AND at least one outlet's capacity known) => C_H(U):=min(D_H(U),R_H(U)), terms_present:={R,D}, unchanged from v1/v2; (d) neither resolves (no pumps AND no outlet-capacity known) => REFUSED (OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN), terms_present:={}. Every readout of S_H(U) MUST report terms_present alongside the ratio so a reader can see which physical constraint (river outlet, pump station, or both) the number reflects -- this is additive disclosure, not a new refusal path. binding(U) is redefined identically over C_H(U) in place of the old min(D_H,R_H): OUTLET when R_H is the (sole or smaller) resolved term, PUMP when D_H is, and 'both' is unreachable by construction once terms_present has one element.
definitions.cov: v3 NEW (founder ruling 2026-09-27, verbatim: "ทำทั้งหมดให้ระดับโลก แต่พอใช้ได้แม้ข้อมูลไม่ครบ อย่าลืมว่าระบบนี้ออกมาสำหรับวิกฤต บางอย่างมันอาจไม่สมบูรณ์ ขอแค่ข้อมูลจริงแม้เล็กที่สุดในบางสถานการณ์ ก็ยังดี" -- 'built for a crisis; something being incomplete is fine, even the smallest real datum in some situations is still worth something). The coverage vector cov(U) is a 7-tuple, each component in {present, stale, absent}, checked independently of the R_H/D_H/F_H ledger above: (rain_obs, rain_fcst, canal_level_vs_lines, river_flow_vs_cap, dam_release, pumps_state, upstream_inflow). 'present' = a reading exists and is within its declared staleness window (3h live / 24h forecast, per unit_resolution.staleness_and_ensemble_defaults); 'stale' = a reading exists but is past its window; 'absent' = no reading at all. cov is a pure input-availability readout, orthogonal to whether the FULL S_H/T_act ledger above happens to be computable from what IS present.
definitions.coverage_score: v3 NEW: a plain count, MEASURED, never a probability or a confidence value -- coverage_score(U) := |{c in cov(U) : c = present}| / 7. Reported alongside every PARTIAL readout (and, for transparency, alongside FULL/LR readouts too) so a reader can see how much of the declared input surface was actually available, independent of which tier came out. v5 AMENDMENT: the denominator is now 10 (cov5), not 7 -- see cov5 below; the v3/v4 definition and every value it was ever reported against a 7-wide cov(U) remains historically correct for that reading, it is simply superseded going forward by cov5's wider denominator.
definitions.tau_up: v5 NEW (founder instruction 2026-09-27, verbatim: "ถึงจะแม่นยำและใช้ได้กับทุกสถานที่" -- accurate AND usable everywhere -- responding to the backtest finding that all v4 inputs are IN-UNIT and therefore lag the flood rather than leading it, per thailand_flood_kg docs/BACKTEST_PROP_FLOOD_06_v1.md sec.4/9: Hat Yai X.44 never crossed L3 across two real events, Nan N.1 first-warned -48h after onset, Chiang Mai P.1 0h, and only the upstream-inflow-dominated Ayutthaya got real lead time, at a 51.6% false-alarm cost). tau_up(U) is the declared travel time, in hours, from the designated UPSTREAM gauge(s) of U to U itself: the hydraulic/hydrologic lag between a rise at the upstream point and its arrival at U. Declared per unit, e.g. N.64 (Tha Wang Pha, upstream of Nan town on the Nan river) for Nan town per DATA_SWEEP_2026-09-27.md sec 'N.1/N.64'; P.67/P.75 (upstream of P.1/Chiang Mai on the Ping river) IF THEY EXIST -- this proposal does NOT assert they exist, DATA_SWEEP_2026-09-27.md records no confirmed reading for either code, so Chiang Mai's tau_up is REFUSED (UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED, a v5-new refusal code scoped to this term only, see refusal codes) until a real upstream gauge is confirmed; X.90/X.173 above the R.1 (Khlong U-Taphao) intake for Hat Yai -- X.90 is confirmed present in DATA_SWEEP (used there only as a downstream CONTROL station, not yet re-purposed as an upstream leading gauge, so its suitability as UPSTREAM for this promoter is itself OPEN, not assumed), X.173 is undeclared/unconfirmed in this repo's own knowledge base; C.2 -> C.13 for Ayutthaya (upstream Chao Phraya reach into the C.13/Bang Ban reach) -- C.2's existence/telemetry is likewise unconfirmed in DATA_SWEEP_2026-09-27.md, so this pairing is OPEN, not asserted. tau_up itself is OPEN-until-measured for every unit named above: no value is declared here, only the DECLARATION SLOT and, where a real gauge is confirmed (N.64), which gauge fills it. An undeclared tau_up REFUSES only the upstream-leading promoter/lead_time_h term for that unit (UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED), never the whole readout -- exactly the v3/v4 PARTIAL-mode discipline extended to this new term.
definitions.upstream_rise_rate: v5 NEW, cov5 component (a): PROP-FLOOD-01's Delta_k(t) applied to the declared UPSTREAM gauge's own series h_up (not U's own series) -- RISING at a rate exceeding a declared threshold (OPEN-for-founder-tuning, national default TBD, per-unit override via definitions.calibration) is what fires promoter P_UPSTREAM_RISE_RATE_EXCEEDS below. Present in cov5(U) iff the declared upstream gauge has a reading within its staleness window (same 3h-live default as v2/v3); absent when no upstream gauge is declared for U at all (UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED) or its reading is stale/missing.
definitions.basin_rain_accum: v5 NEW, cov5 component (b): rain accumulated over A_U's UPSTREAM sub-basin (the DWR/RID basin polygon feeding into U, not A_U itself) over 24h and 72h windows, from gauges within that upstream polygon plus ERA5/IMERG gap-fill (tagged RELAYED per the founder's 2026-09-27 FloodConnect ruling that OSM/ERA5-class gap-fillers are an allowed RELAYED source, never silently promoted to VERIFIED). Reported as two parallel figures (24h, 72h), never collapsed to one number, mirroring rain_t's existing median/max discipline.
definitions.forecast_rain_72h: v5 NEW, cov5 component (c): the ensemble rainfall forecast (same 'whichever multimodel files are actually present, logged per-run' declaration as v2's rain_resolution) evaluated over the NEXT 72h at U's declared upstream sub-basin, reported as two parallel readouts (ensemble median, ensemble max), never one number -- this is the only genuinely forward-looking (not-yet-observed) term in cov5; it is a forecast, not a retained difference, and inherits ordinary forecast-uncertainty caveats (see honest_caveats v5 addition).
definitions.T_act_upstream / lead_time_h: v5 NEW: a projected time-to-threshold, reusing PROP-FLOOD-02's construction (T_k := (theta-h(t))*k/Delta_k(t), REFUSED-as-non-value discipline unchanged) applied to the UPSTREAM series h_up shifted by tau_up(U) -- i.e. h(t):=h_up(t - tau_up(U)), theta:=the upstream gauge's own declared threshold (its own critical/warning line, not U's C_H(U)/F_H(U) ledger). This is what actually gives lead time: because h_up is evaluated tau_up hours before it would arrive at U, a crossing projected from it is a genuine advance warning, not a same-time or lagging one. REFUSED (UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED) when tau_up(U) or the declared upstream gauge itself is undeclared; REFUSED (UNRESOLVED/NOT_APPLICABLE, reusing PROP-FLOOD-02's own two reason codes verbatim) under the same conditions PROP-FLOOD-02 already declares (falling, already past threshold, or NO_READOUT). Reported in the readout record as lead_time_h : option Q -- None on any REFUSED branch, Some(hours) otherwise; never fabricated as a fixed constant when the upstream series does not license one.
definitions.calibration_procedure: v5 NEW (declared falsifier discipline, not a fit that claims truth): for a unit U with recorded history (real observed events with ground truth, e.g. thailand_flood_kg's events.yaml), calibration chooses this unit's own band edges (on S_H, T_act) and promoter thresholds (rain_24h_mm, upstream_rise_rate rate, canal lines, etc.) from a FINITE, predeclared candidate grid (all values in Q, e.g. S_H edges from {0.1, 0.2, ..., 2.0} step 0.1, rain thresholds from {40,50,...,150}mm step 10 -- the grid itself must be stated per unit, never chosen after seeing which value 'worked'), by MAXIMISING observed hits subject to a DECLARED max false-alarm-rate ceiling (e.g. FA <= 15%, itself a declared, not silently chosen, constant) over the unit's own recorded event history. The chosen values, plus the MEASURED hit/FA/median-lead-time they produced on that same history, are recorded as the unit's own `calibration` block (see readout_classes.calibration below), tagged MEASURED-on-backtest, dated, and append-only (a version LIST, never an overwritten single value -- exactly PROP-FLOOD-06's own .v<k> lineage discipline, applied per-unit rather than per-proposal). FALSIFIER DISCIPLINE (the rule that makes this a genuine calibration rather than curve-fitting dressed as one): a unit may be RE-calibrated only when a NEW real event (previously unseen ground truth, not already in the candidate grid's fitting set) becomes available -- re-running the same finite grid against the SAME already-fitted data twice, without new ground truth, is explicitly PROHIBITED and must be refused/flagged by whoever runs the procedure, not silently permitted. This is the same discipline PROP-FLOOD-06's own falsifier section already states for the proposal as a whole (a systematic tier/outcome mismatch falsifies calibration, not the arithmetic), applied per-unit and per-recalibration-event.
definitions.calibrated: v5 NEW readout field, bool-shaped in the schema but carrying a structured value: calibrated: yes(n_events, hit, FA, median_lead_h) when a unit has been through calibration_procedure at least once (n_events = size of the fitting ground-truth set, hit/FA/median_lead_h = the MEASURED-on-backtest values the chosen thresholds produced) | no ("ยังไม่สอบเทียบที่นี่" -- not yet calibrated here -- meaning this unit's readout uses the NATIONAL DEFAULT thresholds, i.e. exactly v1-v4's declared OPEN-for-founder-tuning constants, unchanged). No unit registered by this v5 bump has actually been calibrated yet (empirical_test_status remains 'none' at registration time) -- every worked/backtest unit in this proposal (Hat Yai, Nan, Chiang Mai, Ayutthaya, Bangkok East) is `calibrated: no` until a founder-approved calibration run against calibration_procedure is separately conducted and recorded.
definitions.hysteresis_p_q: v5 NEW (false-alarm control, founder's task-brief instruction): a promoter/band candidate raise must hold for `p` CONSECUTIVE hourly readouts (declared, default p=2) before the reported tier actually steps up; a tier only steps DOWN after `q` consecutive readouts at or below the lower level (declared, default q=3). Both are declared conventions, OPEN-for-founder-tuning exactly like the S_H/T_act band edges, NOT derived. This explicitly trades lead time for false-alarm rate: holding p>=2 delays every raise by at least (p-1) hours relative to the un-persisted (raw) rule, which is a cost against Nan/Chiang Mai's already-thin or negative lead time (see BACKTEST_PROP_FLOOD_06_v1.md sec.4) -- both the achieved lead-time reduction AND the false-alarm-rate improvement MUST be reported side by side in any backtest of this rule, never one without the other. Formalised in Coq as `persisted` (coq/canonical/PROP_FLOOD_06_outlet_coping_tier.v, v5 section): `persisted_is_some_historical_raw` proves persistence never fabricates a tier absent from the raw (un-persisted) history -- it can only delay a raise/lowering that the raw rule already produced at some earlier or the same hour, never invent a new one. v6 AMENDMENT: `persisted_v6` fixes r3's MUST-FIX -- a raise INTO T_L5 (system already exceeded) or T_LR (REFUSED) now bypasses the p-consecutive-readout gate entirely and is reported immediately; a lowering, including a lowering OUT OF T_L5/T_LR, is UNCHANGED, still gated on q. Proved: `persisted_v6_L5_immediate`, `persisted_v6_LR_immediate`, and `persisted_v6_is_some_historical_raw` (the v5 guarantee, kept, with the bypass).

Proved: `upstream_leading_state_value_iff_in_range_and_declared` (a value is reported only when tau_up is declared AND the shifted index is in range).

readout_classes.tier_ladder: REPLACES a bare 3-band S_H convention with a declared >=5-level ladder combining S_H(U) (severity) and T_act(U) (urgency), per founder instruction 2026-09-27 that a resident needs to know 'act now vs. there is still time', not severity alone. v2 AMENDMENT (per independent review, MUST-FIX #3): precedence is now stated as a single total, unambiguous order, replacing the v1 text's unresolved overlap between the L5 pre-check and the 'S_H:=0, OK' case -- both shared the same (D_H,R_H,P_U)-only trigger and differed only by F_H, which v1 never stated as the actual discriminator. The order is: (i) LR -- checked first, if any refusal code fired (see readout_classes.refusal); (ii) L5 -- else if min(D_H,R_H)=0 AND F_H(U)>0 (the exhausted-system-with-still-arriving-inflow case), OR the unit's own gauged level reading is already above its declared flood threshold at evaluation time; L5's first disjunct is now explicitly gated on F_H>0 -- this is deliberately identical to, and replaces, the former ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW refusal code, which is REMOVED from the refusal list in this v2 (see honest_caveats): 'the system is already exceeded' is a valid readout for residents, not a non-evaluable input state, so it is promoted from a refusal to a tier; (iii) else the ordinary band rule over (S_H,T_act): whichever of the S_H-band or T_act-band is HIGHER (later/more urgent in the ladder below) governs the reported level; both sub-readouts are always shown alongside the governing level, never only the combined level. This branch (iii) also covers the case min(D_H,R_H)=0 AND F_H(U)=0: per definitions.S_H(U), the caller sets S_H(U):=0 in that case (no capacity declared and none needed), which the band rule below places in L0 exactly as intended -- no separate rule is needed for it once (ii) is gated on F_H>0. Ladder bands for (iii): S_H<0.3 and T_act>H -> L0 ('ปกติ'); 0.3<=S_H<0.6 or T_act>48h -> L1 ('เฝ้าดู'); 0.6<=S_H<0.9 or 24h<T_act<=48h -> L2 ('เตรียมตัวได้ ยังมีเวลา'); 0.9<=S_H<1.2 or 6h<T_act<=24h -> L3 ('ทำตอนนี้ภายในวันนี้'); S_H>=1.2 or T_act<=6h -> L4 ('เร่งด่วนเดี๋ยวนี้'); each band's stated lower bound (0.3/0.6/0.9/1.2) is CLOSED (belongs to the upper band), matching coq/canonical/PROP_FLOOD_06_outlet_coping_tier.v's `s_band` exactly (fixed per independent review MUST-FIX #2, which found the v1 Coq had these boundaries inverted). The verbs attached to each Thai label above (e.g. ยังมีเวลาค่อยๆทำ vs เร่งด่วนเดี๋ยวนี้) are FloodConnect application wording, not part of this proposal's declared numbers -- this object defines only the thresholds and the level identifiers L0..L5/LR. Formalised as the single total function `full_tier` in coq/canonical/PROP_FLOOD_06_outlet_coping_tier.v over (refused, D_H, R_H, F_H, S_H, T_act); totality and decidability are proved there (`full_tier_total`, `tier_level6_eq_dec`), though the 'gauged level already above threshold' disjunct of (ii) remains unformalised (IO-shaped, OPEN, see that file's header). v3 AMENDMENT: every occurrence of 'min(D_H(U),R_H(U))' in the L5 pre-check and in the ordinary S_H(U) computation above is now C_H(U) (definitions.C_H(U)) -- a total case split that resolves the no-pump contradiction the backtest found (thailand_flood_kg BACKTEST_PROP_FLOOD_06_v0.md sec.2.1, RELAYED). full_tier's zero-capacity pre-check likewise now reads zero_capacity(C_H) rather than zero_capacity(D,R); see the Coq file's v3 section.

readout_classes.refusal: REFUSED with reason in {UNIT_NOT_DECLARED, UNIT_POLYGON_MISSING, OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, NO_GAUGE_IN_UNIT, MISSING_INPUT, STALE_INPUT, UNDECLARED_AREA, UNDECLARED_EDGE, DERATING_UNDECLARED} (NO_PUMPS_IN_UNIT is declared explicitly NOT a refusal code -- it is the valid D_H(U):=0 case; ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW is REMOVED from this list in v2 -- see readout_classes.tier_ladder, it is now the L5 tier, not a refusal). Precedence, checked in this fixed order: (1) UNIT_NOT_DECLARED / UNIT_POLYGON_MISSING -- the (lat,lon)-resolution step cannot produce a usable tuple at all; (2) OUTLET_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN / NO_GAUGE_IN_UNIT -- the tuple resolved but a specific resolved input lacks a value; (3) MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT/DERATING_UNDECLARED -- a declared input exists but its current reading is absent/stale, or a unit has not declared its gravity/tide derating factor g_U(t) (v2: this is now REFUSED rather than silently defaulting to 1 -- see honest_caveats and unit_resolution); (4) UNDECLARED_AREA/UNDECLARED_EDGE -- reused verbatim from PROP-FLOOD-03. LR (REFUSED) in the tier ladder fires whenever any of these codes fires, and always outranks every numeric L0..L5 band; the former (5) ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW slot is now the L5 tier check, run only after LR is ruled out (see readout_classes.tier_ladder). v5 ADDITION: a sixth refusal code, UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED, is scoped ONLY to the leading upstream-rise-rate promoter and lead_time_h (definitions.tau_up/T_act_upstream) -- it fires when U has no declared upstream gauge and/or no declared tau_up, and REFUSES only that term (upstream_rise_rate's cov5 component is reported absent, and lead_time_h:=null), never the unit's whole readout the way the other five codes can; this mirrors the v3/v4 PARTIAL-mode discipline (one missing input degrades gracefully, it does not refuse everything) applied specifically to the new leading term. v6 AMENDMENT: a seventh refusal code, UPSTREAM_TAU_UNDECLARED, is added, scoped identically -- it fires when U HAS a declared upstream gauge but tau_up itself is not declared (previously folded silently into UPSTREAM_GAUGE_UNDECLARED); the two codes are now distinguished (gauge missing vs. gauge present but travel time missing), still refusing only the leading term, never the whole readout. See definitions.upstream_leading_boundary.
readout_classes.mode: v3 NEW, v4 AMENDED: every full_tier readout now carries mode in {FULL, PARTIAL, LR} (LR unchanged from v2's refusal state, checked LAST in v4 -- see the "ข้อมูลเพิ่มไม่เคยลดระดับ" (more data never lowers the level) discipline in the Coq monotonicity theorems below -- per the founder's crisis-priority ruling that a tier must be returned whenever ANY real input exists -- refusal is reserved for when NONE does). v4 REPLACES v3's exclusive (i)/(ii)/(iii) mode-selection order (which let PARTIAL and FULL each consult a DIFFERENT, disjoint source of truth -- the promoter table only in PARTIAL, the S_H/T_act bands only in FULL -- see honest_caveats' v4 note on the round-2 finding this fixed) with a FLOOR order that every mode always shares: (1) band_tier := full_tier's S_H/T_act combined_tier if the ledger resolves (FULL), else L0 (PARTIAL/no-ledger case contributes no band term, not a penalty -- see readout_classes.tier_ladder); (2) promoter_max := the MAXIMUM tier level over every promoter in readout_classes.promoter_table whose own required cov component is present, in EVERY mode, not only PARTIAL (a promoter whose input is stale/absent simply does not enter the max); (3) base_tier := max(band_tier, promoter_max) -- FULL mode's ledger tier and the promoter floor are now always combined, never mutually exclusive; (4) the vulnerable-unit +1 rule (VULNERABLE_UNIT_PROMOTION) applies to base_tier identically regardless of mode; (5) LR overrides the result of (1)-(4) entirely, and ONLY fires iff cov(U) is entirely absent or entirely stale-beyond-window across all 7 components -- checked LAST, per this v4 amendment's explicit ordering (in v3 LR was checked first; the observable result is unchanged since LR still dominates, but the ordering is now stated to match the actual monotonicity proof in Coq, which reasons about the non-LR case, then applies LR as a separate override). mode itself is reported as FULL when the ledger resolves and cov(U) is not entirely absent, PARTIAL when the ledger does not resolve but cov(U) has at least one present component, and LR when cov(U) is entirely absent/stale, exactly as v3 already declared. Every PARTIAL readout carries: mode:'PARTIAL', based_on: [the cov(U) component names present], missing: [every other cov(U) component], coverage_score (definitions.coverage_score), and which promoter(s) fired -- now MANDATORY, structural fields of the return value (readout_schema below), not droppable prose. This is a total function of cov(U) and the promoter table: every cov(U) falls into exactly one of LR/FULL/PARTIAL by the case split above, and the promoter floor is a total max over a finite promoter list (empty max is defined as L0, never undefined).

claim_boundary: This is a finite bookkeeping ratio over declared readouts and declared static constants, not a hydraulic/hydrological simulation: no channel routing, no unsteady-flow (Saint-Venant) solve, no rainfall-runoff model beyond the single declared scalar c_U (or its bound pair) is asserted. Q_cap,o is a DECLARED capacity constant (e.g. 3,000-3,100 m^3/s for the Bangkok Chao Phraya reach, tagged RELAYED -- relayed from a capacity note, not independently re-measured here) and must carry its own source tag wherever instantiated; using it without a tag is a protocol violation, not a licensed use of this object. g_U(t) (v2) is never a silent default: an undeclared g_U(t) is REFUSED (DERATING_UNDECLARED); when a unit explicitly declares g_U(t)=1 (e.g. Bangkok), that declared 1 is a stated assumption, not a measured pump/tide-interaction curve, and must be reported with its OPEN flag. The tier boundaries (OK/TIGHT/CRITICAL) are a declared convention for human triage, not a derived flood-onset boundary; they carry no claim that CRITICAL implies flooding or that OK implies safety. The upstream-inflow term Q_in,up is only as complete as U's declared graph edges, exactly as PROP-FLOOD-03's Q_in discipline requires -- an undeclared upstream contribution is refused, never silently zeroed.

parents.evidence: Q_cap,o - Q_o,now (the per-outlet headroom margin) is a retained difference between a declared static capacity and a currently sampled reading, composed additively across outlets and multiplied by a finite horizon H*3600 -- the same root primitive (delta_R = (a sharp b), Th_coqc per readout_genesis Part I) that PROP-FLOOD-01/03/04 already cite, here applied to a capacity-vs-flow margin rather than a temporal trend or a spatial head-gradient.

PROP-FLOOD-03's finite water-balance ledger (S_b(k+1) := S_b(k) + P(k)*A_b*c_b + Q_in(k)*tau - Q_out(k)*tau, on Q, with an explicit REFUSED discipline for MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT/UNDECLARED_AREA/UNDECLARED_EDGE/NEGATIVE_STORAGE) is the direct parent of this proposal's F_H(U) rainfall-runoff term (c_U*A_U*rain, PROP-FLOOD-03's P(k)*A_b*c_b term summed over H) and of its refusal-code discipline (UNDECLARED_AREA, UNDECLARED_EDGE reused verbatim; STALE_INPUT/MISSING_INPUT reused verbatim). This proposal does not re-derive the tick-by-tick ledger; it aggregates a horizon-H forecast volume from the same declared per-tick shape and adds a distinct outlet-capacity term (R_H) and pump-clearance term (D_H) that PROP-FLOOD-03 does not itself construct.

T_act(U) is a direct reuse of PROP-FLOOD-02's time-to-threshold-by-linear-extension construction (T_k := (theta-h(t))*k/Delta_k(t), defined only while rising toward theta, REFUSED otherwise), instantiated with a time-varying threshold theta:=min(D_t,R_t) and h(t):=F_t(U) in place of a single fixed theta and a single sensor series; PROP-FLOOD-02's REFUSED-as-non-value discipline is also the precedent for this proposal's own ZERO_CAPACITY_NONZERO_INFLOW refusal (when min(D_H,R_H)=0 and F_H>0, S_H(U) would be an unbounded ratio, reported as REFUSED per the workspace's zero-infinity non-readout guard, never as +infinity or a maximal CRITICAL number). v5 ADDITION: PROP-FLOOD-02's construction is reused a SECOND time in v5, applied to the declared UPSTREAM gauge's own series shifted by the declared travel time tau_up (theta:=the upstream gauge's own declared threshold, h(t):=the upstream gauge reading at t-tau_up) to produce lead_time_h -- a genuinely distinct instantiation from T_act(U) itself (which stays defined on U's own in-unit F_t/C_H series), not a restatement or a silent replacement of it.

v5 ADDITION (new parent, previously cited only in this proposal's MD prose, not this JSON parents array): upstream_rise_rate (definitions.upstream_rise_rate) is a direct, unmodified instantiation of PROP-FLOOD-01's Delta_k(t) := h(t) - h(t-k) lag-k retained-difference construction, applied to the declared UPSTREAM gauge's own series h_up(t) (not U's own in-unit series), with PROP-FLOOD-01's own RISING/FALLING/FLAT/NO_READOUT four-way partition reused verbatim as the promoter's fires condition (RISING at rate exceeding a declared threshold).
